requested.title: PR-head repository instructions can reach the privileged agent

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The PR clone is explicitly checked out at the attacker-controlled PR head in `clonePullRequest`, while `pr-base` is fetched only as a tag. `readRepoInstructions(host, "pr")` correctly uses `readFileAtRef(host, PR_BASE_TAG, path)`, and its dedicated test proves that a head-only root `AGENTS.md` is excluded. However, `runOpencodeTurn` always starts `servedInstructionsFile(host, deps.writeFile)` without passing or considering `job.anchor`. That helper runs `find` in the checked-out working tree and then reads every discovered `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, including nested files, with `readWorkFile`, which resolves directly to that PR-head working tree. `formatServedInstructions` preserves the arbitrary content and `opencodeServerEnv` passes the generated harness file in OpenCode's `instructions` array, whose contents are added to the model system message. Thus, a fork contributor can add a root or nested instruction file containing a prompt-injection payload and have it supplied to the PR-review agent despite the base-only protection for the bootstrap path. The BOUNDARY text is useful model guidance but does not prevent the attacker-controlled content from entering the privileged model context or enforce tool-level constraints against instructions the model follows. Git history confirms that commit `633ccfe9` added the anchor-aware `readRepoInstructions` protection, while the later served-instructions implementation still reads the working tree; existing supervisor tests cover normal and nested serving but no PR-head exclusion.
